contract.request: POST JSON/form/multipart: username+password without token selects password admission; username+token+backend selects social admission, even with password present. Raw values and OTP presence are preserved for ordered service validation.
contract.response: The root composes session/rate/REST admission and credential/response/finalization services. Forty-one password/social HTTP scenarios prove declared response bodies and signed-token/cookie delivery, including an avatar. Sixteen password and sixteen cross-identity social requests pass concurrently per backend. Full image registry and all supported input/resource/transport behavior remain incomplete.
contract.errors: Credential/OTP and social selection error precedence is characterized. Unknown account returns 401 invalid credential (not found); ambiguous/inactive selection 401 invalid credentials. After candidate selection: unsupported backend 400, invalid social token 401, email mismatch 401, non-string provider email server error. Missing/wrong-length OTP returns 401 OTP code required.; six-character mismatch returns 401 OTP code not valid.; non-sized OTP or corrupt secret reached during verification raises a server error. The registered handler maps these errors. Focused actual-server tests verify password/OTP denials and generic 500 failures without token/cookie delivery; broader provider/input failures remain open.
contract.authentication: AllowAny still authenticates supplied Bearer credentials. Existing cache-session audit precedes shared IP/account rate limits, then REST negotiation, Bearer/scope and body admission. Nineteen ordinary and five rate-ordering methods, sixteen password and sixteen cross-identity social concurrent requests pass on actual servers. Remaining global middleware, historical credential/resource and provider transport gates remain incomplete.
contract.side_effects: Password stage: all matching obsolete Django hashes are upgraded, including ambiguous/inactive outcomes; raw bcrypt only migrates the selected candidate before active-status rejection. Username normalization now creates the existing user update audit and optional association index before OTP; OTP denial retains those writes. Actor and logging-in account remain separate. Membership-card response construction now reads the lowest-UUID existing configuration or creates a default plus create audit and direct association index. Superusers/athletes do not create configurations; collaborators use their connected owner. A separate finalization service atomically updates last_login and cancels current/future UTC delete_on with User audit/index; it is wired into the public HTTP workflow. Declared effects are read back using Django; complete failure/race parity remains open.
contract.transaction: Go credential stage uses bounded keyset pages and batched writes inside a repeatable-read snapshot; only actual password writes lock rows; expected denials commit documented upgrades, infrastructure failures roll back. Serialization/deadlock conflicts retry at most three times. Django partial writes on exceptional failures are deliberately replaced by this atomic boundary. Whole-login transaction coordination remains open. Username/audit/index writes use a separate row-locked atomic transaction with at most three deadlock/serialization retries. This deliberately rolls back orphan pre-save audits that Django can leave after a username uniqueness failure; exact failure-side-effect parity is not claimed. Configuration/audit/index creation is an explicit read-committed transaction with a scoped parent lock and at most three conflict retries; finalization has its own row-locked user/audit/index transaction; whole-login composition is wired, while cross-runtime creation coordination remains open.

evidence: 21 explicit Django actual-view versus Go service account-selection/password-write cases using production hashers; Django verifies Go-written hashes and all managed model tables are compared after restoring declared test changes. 46 explicitly expected Django-rendered base profile versus Go cases on the same private PostgreSQL; all managed tables unchanged after declared fixture restoration. One/two SELECTs regardless of 0/1/2/128/512 onboarding rows; 32 concurrent association reads use 64 SELECTs and release the four-connection pool. Current preference transitions, cancellation and no-partial-profile behavior are tested. This is component evidence, not portable login HTTP parity.

Real PostgreSQL denied-SELECT roles prove optional onboarding failure returns the complete base profile with null onboarding, while required association group failure returns no profile. Both boundaries are characterized through Django; Go releases the aborted transaction and reuses the pool.

23 explicitly expected association profile JSON/outcome cases compare Django serializer/DRF rendering with Go on the same private PostgreSQL. All 50 fields, exact decimal text, PostgreSQL scale rounding, null/scalar JSON, reviewed boundary and deleted/inactive owner semantics are checked. Group counts 0/1/16/128/512 use two SELECTs; 32 concurrent 512-group reads use 64 SELECTs. A deletion/restoration transition is immediately visible; all managed tables match after restoration.

20 explicit actual Django login-response-builder/audit middleware versus Go membership-card cases; exact configuration/audit/index fields and Django readback. Existing/duplicate rows use two statements, creation five; 32 concurrent Go calls create one invariant in 67 statements. Real permission/FK failures, injected errors, cancellation and an observed PostgreSQL audit-actor deadlock verify rollback/retry. Every managed table and SQL-NULL distinction matches after resets.

17 explicit actual Django password-login versus Go finalization cases cover UTC deletion-date boundaries, exact last_login and audit/index readback. Two/four/five-statement paths, 32 concurrent Go calls in 67 statements, real permission/FK failures, injected failures and cancellation verify atomicity and pool release. Django partial autocommit and stale-save overwrites are characterized separately; all managed tables match after restoration.

36 explicitly expected actual Django builder versus Go composed-response cases on shared private PostgreSQL, including all key presence, role-0 behavior, feature masks, exact JSON settings, instructor cardinalities 0/1/2/128/512 and default configuration write/readback. Existing association/collaborator responses use seven statements; creation ten; 32 concurrent compositions use 224 statements on four connections. Real required-instructor permission failures and persisted transitions are tested; all managed tables match after restoration. Image conversion is deliberately outside these cases. Twenty-eight boolean values and eight dotenv cases are characterized with Django and checked in Go.

Image prerequisites: ten explicitly expected actual-Django-helper size decisions, 54 exact Pillow pixel vectors across six modes and 19,535 CPython Base64 differential vectors pass. Go matches every pixel byte without tolerance, preserves immutable inputs and passes cancellation, logical memory/overflow limits and 32 concurrent transformations. All managed tables remain unchanged. The 54 transformed rasters also match their encoded JPEG bytes. JPEG pixel decoding is covered separately; these checks do not provide the complete image processor.

180 exact Pillow JPEG vectors cover five modes, four deterministic patterns and nine sizes. Metadata/quality/sampling expectations anchor the oracle. Input/output limits, exact output ceilings, malformed native protocol, process failure, environment isolation, timeout, queued/running cancellation and 32 concurrent encodes pass. The shipped static codec also passes the same 180 vectors and native protocol in the actual non-root, read-only, networkless Go image. Tested libjpeg-turbo versions: Pillow 3.1.0, local 3.2.0, image 3.0.4; no other codec/architecture equivalence is assumed.

JPEG decoder: 312 exact pixel/comment cases and 1,556 explicit invalid streams; the actual Django compress_base64 helper agrees on all 1,868 output/fallback cases. Of the decoded cases, 310 re-encode byte-exactly and two preserve long-comment save failure. Progressive/optimized/sampling/RGB/CMYK/YCCK/restart/metadata cases, tolerated corruption, every incomplete prefix of selected baseline/progressive streams and comment ordering/size boundaries are covered. Native framing, exact raster budgets, process failure, queued/running cancellation, timeout and 32 concurrent decodes pass. The shipped non-root read-only/networkless codec passes the same cases. Native sanitizer checks assert exact exit codes and complete frames, so generic error mapping cannot conceal failures. Other formats and full image-service parity remain open.

Lazy JPEG marker phase: 1,352 explicit Pillow recognition outcomes, covering all marker codes, payload truncation, precision/component/quantization semantics, metadata marker checks, comments, pixel warnings/hard limits, ordinary encoded headers and prefixes across the first SOS boundary. Three actual Django header-only passthrough cases retain the original despite undecodable pixels. Go checks consumed-header budgets, immutable/non-aliased metadata, EXIF/comment ordering, MPF offsets, scanning cancellation and 32 concurrent readers. The image rehearsal runs the same marker oracle. Raw metadata retention alone is not full Image.open admission; the subsequent metadata stage is covered separately.

JPEG metadata: 226 explicitly expected EXIF/MPF first-frame outcomes, exact JPEG bytes, directory/record cancellation and 32 concurrent MPO inspections. Complete JPEG file pipeline: 73 explicit disk-size/lazy/fallback cases plus all metadata and 1,868 decoder cases; actual Django helper and shipped non-root read-only/networkless image agree. Per-stage logical budgets, 32 concurrent resizes and whole-pipeline queued/running cancellation with child reaping and admission reuse pass. Other file formats and public login remain open.

PNG compressed pixels: 803 explicit cases compare independently constructed samples with Pillow across 15 depth/color combinations, five filters, Adam7, large buffers and malformed streams. Actual Django helper results distinguish 480 exact unchanged-size JPEG outputs, 300 unsupported-mode fallbacks and 23 invalid-stream fallbacks. Go checks pixel/transform/JPEG composition, exact logical budgets, overflow, mid-decode cancellation and 32 concurrent Adam7 decodes; the non-root read-only/networkless image runs the same oracle. Valid zlib stream ends on complete ordinary/Adam7 rows leave remaining pixels zero; incomplete rows or missing trailers before remaining rows still fail. These cases cover pixel composition; file-level metadata/canvas behavior is covered separately.

PNG lazy header/metadata: 394 explicit Pillow outcomes cover chunk/CRC and metadata payload rules, text inflation/cumulative character ceilings, duplicate headers, APNG frame declarations/sequences/rectangles and text-key collisions. The actual Django helper returns original URIs for 235 valid 200x100 headers with zero pixel loads observed through a delegating loader. Exact consumed-header budgets, metadata ownership, cancellation during text inflation/conversion and 32 concurrent readers pass; the non-root read-only/networkless image runs the same oracle. File-level validation and canvas composition are covered separately; public image wiring remains open. Server transaction drain: each owned Go transaction acquires a separate acknowledged shared transaction advisory lock before effects; all five standalone queue mutations now use that boundary. In-app Django restore and CLI backup/migration take its exclusive form under the file lease before operation/export/snapshot work, with bounded fail-closed waits. Transaction lifetime regression: all 17 explicit repository entrypoints retain a private owned pgx connection through completion and driver/socket cleanup. Eight real PostgreSQL/race groups cover worker, HTTP and snapshot admission plus reuse/concurrent finish/cancelled begin/failed SQL; three representative old-source cases fail before the fix. Server transaction drain: each owned Go transaction acquires a separate acknowledged shared transaction advisory lock before effects; all five standalone queue mutations now use that boundary. Failed cancellation delivery cannot make a fenced remote COMMIT cross the drain barrier. This covers cooperating Go transactions, not every Django writer, provider or older binary. notes: Username-normalization, final-login deletion-cancellation and membership-card default-creation audits are currently implemented in Go. Other registered models, changes-JSON fallbacks, deletion and audit lifecycle operations remain open.

The explicit Go invariant transaction propagates index failures and rolls back username/event/index; Django can suppress index failures or leave pre-save collision events. These failure-side-effect differences remain explicit, not certified as identical parity.

Django concurrent missing configuration lookups can create two rows; denied audit/index inserts retain partial autocommit effects. Go serializes participating Go writers and atomically rolls back the invariant. These differences are explicit; the Go parent lock does not coordinate unmodified Django writers. Cross-runtime concurrent creation remains unimplemented/unverified before activation.

Final-login writes are a separate, unwired service: last_login and qualifying delete_on cancellation with atomic audit/index. Django full-model saves overwrite concurrent password/name/active changes; Go preserves them. End-to-end revocation admission and mixed-runtime audit races remain open. See BE_GO/internal/service/login_finalization.md.
